description: Session-start version check (reports newer releases, safely applies an opted-in repository-scoped update, gives a verified reload handoff; silent when current), a per-session record of the plugin version this session has loaded (written at every session start and every prompt, read by the status line; it also holds the session's live model and effort, noted before each tool call of the main conversation and after each model switch, with one small local read and a write only when one changed, which the planning and build skills compare with the repository's expected ones; at a prompt it also refreshes the newest-release cache in the background when older than 30 minutes and, once per new version, asks Claude to tell or ask the person about a reload or update, changing nothing itself; fails open), a prompt-time session gate (one job class per session: an authoring job and an execution job do not share a session; fails open) and a live-status report for every session, inside a repository or not: through the repository's own presence command when its .claude/ds-config.json names one, else through the built-in reporter, which sends it to DevStride with the API key the machine's DevStride connection carries, else with the machine's session reporter credential (with neither, nothing runs: every session start shows the person a one-line notice, and the first prompt that runs a DevStride skill has the model set the session reporter up; presence set to null switches a repository off and DEVSTRIDE_PRESENCE=0 a machine) (at session start, on prompts and finished turns, throttled, with the time of its last activity, stamped before and after each tool call, and, while the session is inside one call or its finished turn left background work running, since when; it reports waiting while Claude waits on its person: a finished turn, a question, a permission or elicitation prompt, an interrupted turn; and at session end, plus a detached per-session keeper at its interval (a minute for the built-in reporter, five for a command) while the session's process lives, which also reads the end of the session's transcript to find an interrupt, since Claude Code fires no hook for one; the keeper follows the loaded plugin: after an update it is replaced by one of the loaded version, and every report names the version of the code sending it; a repository's command decides what its report means; the built-in reporter sends a short fixed list and never session text, a path or the machine's address, and goes quiet for 30 minutes when the server refuses it over HTTP or has no such tool, and 2 minutes when it cannot be reached, refuses one request with an error that names its reason, or a refusal sets the session reporter credential aside; a new name someone asks for on the Agent Fleet comes back on its answer, is kept on this machine, set as the session's own title at the next prompt, start, resume or fork, as /rename would, and reported as taken once the session carries it; fails open). A session a person stops on the Agent Fleet stops on this machine too: the keeper asks DevStride for a stop every 15 seconds while the session works and every 60 while it waits on its person, every 15 once a stop is kept, and once at the start of a session started again while one is kept (wherever the connection carries a key or the machine has a session reporter credential; an error or a timeout changes nothing), the stop is kept on this machine, and a gate that runs first on every tool call and every prompt refuses them, a helper agent's calls included, with who stopped the session, when and why, until a person allows it to continue on the Agent Fleet; a session running with no person at it (-p or --print, the SDK, or DEVSTRIDE_UNATTENDED=1) is ended as well, once the server knows this machine heard the stop; the gate reads one local file, uses no network and fails open, except that a stop record it cannot read counts as a stop. Only in a repository whose .claude/ds-config.json names a session title command, it also asks that command for a title at session start, resume and fork and at each prompt, and sets it as the session's own title only while the session has no name a person gave it (or the title is the one it set itself, or the command says a person asked for the new one); fails open. A workflow run is driven only where its step agents can be heard: a helper agent is refused the skills that drive a run (release, plan, run-workflow, branch-hotfix and rebalance), anyone is refused a step agent started in the background, and a finished turn of the main conversation that leaves one of the session's runs with a step nothing is running (no agent, workflow or cloud session of the session still running) is held once per run, step and attempt, as is a run stopped for its person's answer, with what to do: carry the run on there, ending the turn again only for a pause the person asked for or a question already shown to them; it reads the step runner's local status with a three-second limit and fails open. Every operation is bounded. Each Python hook starts through hooks/python.sh, which finds Python 3 on Windows too (py -3, python or python3, never the Microsoft Store placeholder) and gives the session's own commands the same python3.
